missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative subject. 'Честь' is a feminine soft-sign noun in the nominative as the subject. 'Важна' is the short feminine adjective agreeing with it.
Strategic focus: Accusative object. 'Честь' is the accusative object of 'защищает'; for this feminine soft-sign noun the accusative matches the nominative. 'Свою' agrees in the feminine accusative.
Strategic focus: Genitive of relation. 'Чести' is the genitive singular after 'вопрос', forming the set phrase 'вопрос чести', meaning a matter of honour.
Strategic focus: Dative after the verb. 'Чести' is the dative singular governed by 'нанести вред', which takes the dative of the affected thing. 'Нельзя' marks the prohibition.
Strategic focus: Instrumental after the verb. 'Честью' is the instrumental singular governed by 'гордиться', which takes the instrumental. 'Своей' agrees in the feminine instrumental.
Strategic focus: Prepositional case. 'Чести' is the prepositional singular after 'о', expressing the topic. 'Семьи' is the genitive showing whose honour it is.
Strategic focus: Accusative in a set phrase. 'Честь' appears in the accusative after 'в' in the idiom 'в честь', meaning in honour of. 'Героев' is the genitive plural complement.
Strategic focus: Accusative in the salute idiom. 'Честь' is the accusative object in the phrase 'отдать честь', meaning to salute. 'Генералу' is the dative recipient.
Strategic focus: Accusative in a polite formula. 'Честь' is the accusative object of 'имею' in the formal phrase 'имею честь', meaning I have the honour. 'Гостя' is the animate accusative.

missions.phrase: В армии много понятий о чести.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Prepositional case after a quantity phrase. 'Чести' is the prepositional singular after 'о', linked to 'много понятий', where 'понятий' is the genitive plural after 'много'.
